Package edu.cnu.mdi.graphics.rubberband

Class ARubberband

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.graphics.rubberband.ARubberband
All Implemented Interfaces:
MouseListener, MouseMotionListener, EventListener
Direct Known Subclasses:
AClickRubberband, ADragRubberband
public abstract class ARubberband extends Object implements MouseListener, MouseMotionListener
Base class for all rubberband gestures. Owns: - lifecycle (start/end/cancel) - image buffering + overlay drawing - shared points (start/current) - shared poly storage (poly/tempPoly) for click-collected gestures Subclasses own: - interaction semantics (drag vs click) - shape drawing - bounds + vertices + validity rules (if not area-based)

  • Method Details

    • begin

      public final void begin(Point anchorPt)
      Begin rubberbanding with the given anchor point. For drag-based policies, this is typically called from mousePressed(); for toolbar-initiated gestures, this is called by the toolbar to start the gesture with a specific anchor point.
      Parameters:
      anchorPt - the initial point of the gesture, which may be used as the start point and for initial drawing; may be null but is typically not.

    • isActive

      public final boolean isActive()
      Active means listening and rubberbanding in response to mouse events.
      Returns:
      true if this rubberband is active and responding to mouse events, false if inactive or completed (waiting for toolbar to read results).

    • setActive

      public final void setActive(boolean b)
      Activate or deactivate this rubberband. Deactivated rubberbands ignore mouse events and do not draw.
      Parameters:
      b - true to activate, false to deactivate. Deactivation is not the same as completion; it simply ignores mouse events and stops drawing until reactivated or completed.

    • isClickBased

      public boolean isClickBased()
      True if this rubberband collects points on click rather than drag. Used by toolbars to determine when to call isGestureValid() and getRubberbandVertices().
      Returns:
      true if this rubberband collects points on click rather than drag, false if it is drag-based.

    • isGestureValid

      public boolean isGestureValid(int minSizePx)
      Validity rules depend on the policy; default is area-based (bounds must exceed min size). Click-based policies should override with their own rules.
      Parameters:
      minSizePx - minimum size in pixels for validity; interpretation depends on policy (e.g. max dimension for polygons).
      Returns:
      true if the current gesture state is valid for completion, false if it should be rejected (e.g. too small).

    • getStart

      public final Point getStart()
      Get the anchor point where the gesture started. For click-based policies, this may be the first click or a synthetic point; for drag-based policies, this is the initial mouse press location.
      Returns:
      the start point of the gesture, which may be used as a reference for drawing and bounds calculations.

    • getCurrent

      public final Point getCurrent()
      Get the current point of the gesture, which may be updated during dragging or clicking. For click-based policies, this may be the most recent click location or a synthetic point; for drag-based policies, this is the current mouse location during dragging.
      Returns:
      the current point of the gesture, which may be used as a reference for drawing and bounds calculations.

    • setFillColor

      public final void setFillColor(Color color)
      Set the fill color for this rubberband. Used for the main shape fill; subclasses may also use it for borders or highlights.
      Parameters:
      color - the fill color to use when drawing this rubberband; may be null for no fill.

    • setHighlightColor1

      public final void setHighlightColor1(Color c)
      Primary highlight color, used for borders or 1-color gradients.
      Parameters:
      c - the primary highlight color to use when drawing this rubberband; may be null if not used.

    • setHighlightColor2

      public final void setHighlightColor2(Color c)
      Secondary highlight color, used for 2-color gradients or borders.
      Parameters:
      c - the secondary highlight color to use when drawing this rubberband; may be null if not used.

    • cancel

      public void cancel()
      Cancel the rubberbanding operation. Discards results and releases resources immediately. The toolbar will not call doneRubberbanding() after this, so the rubberband should not rely on that for cleanup.

    • endRubberbanding

      public void endRubberbanding(Point p)
      Normal completion. Preserves results long enough for the toolbar to read them in IRubberbanded.doneRubberbanding().
      Parameters:
      p - the final point of the gesture, which may be used for final drawing and bounds calculations; may be null if not applicable.

    • getRubberbandBounds

      public abstract Rectangle getRubberbandBounds()
      Get the bounding rectangle of the rubberband shape based on the current state. Used for area-based validity checks and as a default for vertex calculations. Subclasses should override this if their shape is not well-represented by a bounding rectangle (e.g. lines, polygons).
      Returns:
      the bounding rectangle of the rubberband shape, or null if not applicable.

    • getRubberbandVertices

      public final Point[] getRubberbandVertices()
      Get the vertices of the rubberband shape for click-based policies. For drag-based policies, this returns the corners of the bounding rectangle by default.
      Returns:
      an array of points representing the vertices of the rubberband shape, or null if not applicable. For click-based policies, this should return the collected vertices; for drag-based policies, this returns the corners of the bounding rectangle by default.
